title: Custom data forms
summary: Building your own forms for information this product does not model.
html:
Custom data lets you build your own forms and store records in them. It is the escape hatch for information the product does not have a place for: equipment registers, inspection records, membership details, anything specific to your trade.

Before using it

Check whether extra fields will do instead. If the information belongs to a customer or a job — one value per record — an extra field is simpler and appears right on the record. Custom data is for things that are records in their own right, with many of them.

Building a form

  1. Create a data type. This is the form: give it a name and whether it links to a customer.
  2. Add fields. Text, number, date, dropdown, checkbox and so on. Each field has a name and a label.
  3. Group the fields, if the form is long enough to want sections.

Entering and finding records

Once the type exists it gets its own menu entry. Records are created, listed and searched there. You choose which fields appear as columns in the list, which is worth setting — the default columns are rarely the ones you want to scan.

Embedding a form on your website

A data form can be embedded on your own site so people fill it in themselves and the records land here. Embed on the data type screen gives you the code.

Be careful with this: it is a public form writing to your database. Only embed a form you are happy for anyone on the internet to submit, and use a captcha.
